segs.e: Linked Discourses 19.1
Chapter One
A Skeleton
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharanti.
segs.e: Now at that time Venerable Mark and Venerable Mahāmoggallāna were staying on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yenāyasmā lakkhaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ lakkhaṇaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahāmoggallāna robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to Mark and said to him,
“Come, Reverend Mark, let’s enter Rājagaha for alms.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” Mark replied.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto aññatarasmiṁ padese sitaṁ pātvākāsi.
segs.e: As Mahāmoggallāna was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain he smiled at a certain spot.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: So Mark said to Mahāmoggallāna,

segs.p: “ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, Reverend Moggallāna, what is the reason you smiled?”
“Reverend Mark, it’s the wrong time for this question.

segs.p: Bhagavato maṁ santike etaṁ pañhaṁ pucchā”ti.
segs.e: Ask me when we’re in the Buddha’s presence.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca lakkhaṇo āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno rājagahe piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā lakkhaṇo āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mark and Mahāmoggallāna wandered for alms in Rājagaha. After the meal, on their return from almsround, they went to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Mark said to Mahāmoggallāna:

segs.p: “idhāyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto aññatarasmiṁ padese sitaṁ pātvākāsi.
segs.e: “Just now, as Mahāmoggallāna was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain he smiled at a certain spot.

segs.p: Ko nu kho, āvuso moggallāna, hetu ko paccayo sitassa pātukammāyā”ti?
segs.e: What is the cause, Reverend Moggallāna, what is the reason you smiled?”

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ aṭṭhikasaṅkhalikaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantiṁ.
segs.e: “Just now, reverend, as I was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain I saw a skeleton flying through the air.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā phāsuḷantarikāhi vitudenti vitacchenti virājenti.
segs.e: Vultures, crows, and hawks kept chasing it, pecking, clawing, and stabbing it in the ribs
as it screeched in pain.
It occurred to me:
‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!
That there can be such a sentient being,
such a spirit,
such an incarnation!’”
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:
“Mendicants, there are disciples who live full of vision and knowledge,

segs.p: ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti, yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṁ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṁ vā karissati.
segs.e: since a disciple knows, sees, and witnesses such a thing.

segs.p: Pubbeva me so, bhikkhave, satto diṭṭho ahosi, api cāhaṁ na byākāsiṁ.
segs.e: Formerly, I too saw that being, but I did not speak of it.

segs.p: Ahañcetaṁ byākareyyaṁ, pare ca me na saddaheyyuṁ.
segs.e: For if I had spoken of it others would not have believed me,

segs.p: Ye me na saddaheyyuṁ, tesaṁ taṁ assa dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: which would be for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe goghātako ahosi.
segs.e: That being used to be a cattle butcher right here in Rājagaha.

segs.p: So tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesena evarūpaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhaṁ paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti.
segs.e: As a result of that deed he burned in hell for many years, many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands of years. Now he experiences the residual result of that deed in such an incarnation.”
(Tell all these discourses in full like this.)

Linked Discourses 19.9
Chapter One
Needle Hairs (2nd)

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ sūcilomaṁ purisaṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.
segs.e: “Just now, reverend, as I was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain I saw a man whose body hairs were needles flying through the air.

segs.p: Tassa tā sūciyo sīse pavisitvā mukhato nikkhamanti;
segs.e: The needles bored into his head and out his mouth,
into his mouth and out his chest,
into his chest and out his belly,
into his belly and out his thighs,
into his thighs and out his calves,
and into his calves and out his feet.
And he screamed in pain. …” …

segs.p: eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe sūcako ahosi …pe….
segs.e: “That being used to be an informant right here in Rājagaha. …”

segs.e: When he was walking he had to lift his testicles on to his shoulder.
And when he sat down, he sat right on them.

Linked Discourses 19.12
Chapter Two
A Dung Eater

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ purisaṁ gūthakūpe nimuggaṁ ubhohi hatthehi gūthaṁ khādantaṁ …pe…
segs.e: “Just now, reverend, as I was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain I saw a man sunk in a sewer, eating dung with both hands. …” …

segs.p: eso, bhikkhave, satto imasmiṁyeva rājagahe duṭṭhabrāhmaṇo ahosi.
segs.e: “That being used to be a nasty brahmin right here in Rājagaha.

segs.p: So kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane bhikkhusaṅghaṁ bhattena nimantetvā doṇiyo gūthassa pūrāpetvā etadavoca—
segs.e: In the time of the Buddha Kassapa’s dispensation he invited the Saṅgha of mendicants for a meal. He filled a trough with dung and said:

segs.p: aho bhonto yāvadatthaṁ bhuñjantu ceva harantu cā’ti …pe….
segs.e: ‘My good men, eat as much as you like, and take what’s left.’ …”

segs.p: Tassa ure akkhīni ceva honti mukhañca.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ gijjhāpi kākāpi kulalāpi anupatitvā anupatitvā vitacchenti virājenti.

Chapter Two
A Bad Monk

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ bhikkhuṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantaṁ.
segs.e: “Just now, reverend, as I was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain I saw a monk flying through the air.

segs.p: Tassa saṅghāṭipi ādittā sampajjalitā sajotibhūtā, pattopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto, kāyabandhanampi ādittaṁ sampajjalitaṁ sajotibhūtaṁ, kāyopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto.
segs.e: His outer robe, bowl, belt, and body were burning, blazing, and glowing
as he screamed in pain. …” …

segs.p: eso, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane pāpabhikkhu ahosi …pe….
segs.e: “That monk used to be a bad monk in the time of Buddha Kassapa’s dispensation. …”

Linked Discourses 19.21
Chapter Two
A Bad Novice Nun

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohanto addasaṁ sāmaṇeriṁ vehāsaṁ gacchantiṁ.
segs.e: “Just now, reverend, as I was descending from Vulture’s Peak Mountain I saw a novice nun flying through the air.

segs.p: Tassā saṅghāṭipi ādittā sampajjalitā sajotibhūtā, pattopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto, kāyabandhanampi ādittaṁ sampajjalitaṁ sajotibhūtaṁ, kāyopi āditto sampajjalito sajotibhūto.
segs.e: Her outer robe, bowl, belt, and body were burning, blazing, and glowing
as she screamed in pain.
It occurred to me:
‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!
That there can be such a sentient being,
such a spirit,
such an incarnation!’”
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:
“Mendicants, there are disciples who live full of vision and knowledge,

segs.p: ñāṇabhūtā vata, bhikkhave, sāvakā viharanti, yatra hi nāma sāvako evarūpaṁ ñassati vā dakkhati vā sakkhiṁ vā karissati.
segs.e: since a disciple knows, sees, and witnesses such a thing.

segs.p: Pubbeva me sā, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī diṭṭhā ahosi.
segs.e: Formerly, I too saw that novice nun, but I did not speak of it.

segs.p: Ahañcetaṁ byākareyyaṁ, pare ca me na saddaheyyuṁ.
segs.e: For if I had spoken of it others would not have believed me,

segs.p: Ye me na saddaheyyuṁ, tesaṁ taṁ assa dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya.
segs.e: which would be for their lasting harm and suffering.

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, sāmaṇerī kassapassa sammāsambuddhassa pāvacane pāpasāmaṇerī ahosi.
segs.e: That female novice used to be a bad novice nun in the time of the Buddha Kassapa’s dispensation.

segs.p: Sā tassa kammassa vipākena bahūni vassāni bahūni vassasatāni bahūni vassasahassāni bahūni vassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā tasseva kammassa vipākāvasesena evarūpaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhaṁ paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti.
segs.e: As a result of that deed she burned in hell for many years, many hundreds, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands of years. Now she experiences the residual result of that deed in such an incarnation.”
